newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine, IMF reach tentative stand-by agreement-IMF.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine, IMF reach tentative stand-by agreement-IMF.

text.p: Ukraine and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) have agreed in principle on an interim stand-by agreement, the Fund's resident representative Goohoon Kwon said on Tuesday.
"We have reached a tentative agreement, but it is subject to the approval of the authorities of the Fund," Kwon told Reuters. He said an IMF board would review the agreement at the end of next month.
He did not state the value of the one-year deal, which Ukrainian authorities have said would be $750 million.
"That is subject to a decision by the board," Kwon said.

The IMF said this month it would give the credit to Ukraine, whose last stand-by agreement expired in February, as a temporary measure until it fulfilled conditions to qualify for a three-year, $2.5 to $3 billion Extended Fund Facility (EFF).

The former Soviet republic, which began negotiating for the EFF last year, still must meet about 10 of 41 conditions to qualify for the credit aimed at implementing deep structural reform in the economy.
"The (stand-by) arrangement is supposed to be quite temporary. We will quickly move into EFF negotiations," Kwon said.
He said the speed at which talks for the EFF resumed depended on Ukraine's compliance with the stand-by agreement, and could start at the end of this year or early in 1998.
